benchmarks.label: Brent

peak.note: Futures intraday wartime high (Wikipedia chronology). Physical Dated Brent (EIA spot via FRED) peaked at $138.21 on 2026-04-07 and was $114.89 on 2026-09-22.

benchmarks.note: Fell to about $108.82 on 2 Nov (Trading Economics), down roughly 4% on the day and about 4% w/w, after Trump signaled he wants more time for Iran diplomacy before considering further strikes and Secretary of State Rubio said no decision had been made on new strikes (The National, citing Axios/CBS); the remarks came two days before the 3 Nov US midterms. UKMTO reported a separate vessel struck by an unknown projectile in the strait on 1 Nov, a day after the LNG carrier Al Mayeda was hit nearby. Week-ago is this site's 30 Oct reading, 3 days earlier.

note: Brent and WTI each fell more than 3% on 2 November after Trump signaled, per Axios, that he wants more time for Iran diplomacy before considering further strikes; Secretary of State Rubio said a day earlier that no decision had been made on new strikes. TTF eased off its 30 October record close in the same broad selloff. The drop followed UKMTO's report of a vessel struck by an unknown projectile in the Strait of Hormuz on 1 November, a day after the Qatari LNG carrier Al Mayeda was hit nearby despite reported Iranian safe-passage clearance; its crew were unharmed and the ship remained operational. The remarks and the selloff came two days before the 3 November US midterm elections.
